76	## 3. Glossary
77	
78	- **Asset** — A piece of water-main infrastructure Tidewatch tracks (valve, hydrant, backflow-preventer device, or main segment). Has a registered location in the Asset Register.
79	- **Asset Register** — The utility's authoritative GIS system of record for assets (an Esri-compatible feature service), external to Tidewatch. Tidewatch reads from it and proposes write-backs; it does not replace it.
80	- **Inspection Template** — A configurable definition of an inspection type's fields, required evidence, and pass/fail tolerances. V1 ships four: Hydrant Flow Test, Valve Exercise, Main-Break Triage, Backflow-Preventer Test.
81	- **Finding** — A single completed (or in-progress) inspection record produced from an Inspection Template against one Asset.
82	- **Exception** — A Finding that is out-of-tolerance per its template's configured thresholds, or carries an unresolved sync Conflict; the only kind of Finding that enters a supervisor's Review Queue.
83	- **District** — A geographic/organizational grouping of Assets used for route planning, access scoping, and cadence-compliance reporting.
84	- **Route** — A batched set of due/overdue Assets assigned to a Crew for a given day.
85	- **Crew** — One or more field inspectors assigned to a Route, with associated skill certifications and truck equipment.
86	- **Reporting Period** — A date range (e.g., a quarter) used to scope a Regulatory Packet or cadence-compliance view.
87	- **Regulatory Packet** — An exported PDF narrative + CSV data bundle of Findings scoped to a Reporting Period and inspection type, built for submission to a regulator or for internal asset-management reporting.
88	- **Immutable Audit Log** — The append-only record of every create/edit/approve/export action in the system; corrections append new entries with reason codes and never overwrite prior values.
89	- **Provenance** — Per-field metadata (last-editor user ID, device ID, timestamp) retained for every field on every record, feeding both Conflict detection and the Immutable Audit Log.
90	- **Conflict** — A sync-time state where the same field on the same record was changed by two users since their last common sync point; routed to manual merge rather than auto-resolved.
91	- **Sync Cycle** — The process by which a device's queued offline changes are reconciled with the backend, field by field, when connectivity is available.
92	- **Snap-to-Asset** — A one-tap correction that anchors a Finding's location to an Asset's registered location when captured GPS falls within a configured tolerance of it, replacing manual coordinate entry.
93	- **Accuracy Radius** — The reported confidence radius of a GPS fix at time of capture, recorded alongside the coordinates.
94	- **Turn Count / Torque** — Valve Exercise template fields recording how many turns were applied to operate a valve and the torque measured while doing so.
95	- **Cadence Compliance** — The percentage of Assets of a given type inspected within their required/recommended schedule (e.g., valves exercised on time), reportable by District.
96	- **Device-Bound Token** — An authentication token tied to one registered device; revocable independently of the user's account.
97	- **Contractor Account** — A Role-scoped account with a configured expiration date/time and restricted District/Template access, for non-employee field staff.
98	- **Work Order** — A task record in the utility's external work-order system, created from an escalated Finding.
99	
100	## 4. Features
101	
102	### 4.1 Offline-First Sync & Data Integrity
103	
104	**Description:** The foundation the rest of the product depends on: the field app must be fully usable for days with no connectivity, and when connectivity returns, queued changes must reconcile without silently losing an edit or silently overwriting someone else's. Conflict resolution and per-field provenance are specified together because they share one mechanism — a per-field last-writer record is both how a conflict gets detected and how the audit log answers "who touched this." Realizes UJ-1, UJ-4.
105	
106	**Functional Requirements:**
107	
108	#### FR-1: Extended offline operation
109	A field inspector can create, edit, and complete Findings — including photo and signature capture — entirely offline for at least 5 consecutive days.
110	**Consequences (testable):**
111	- All four v1 Inspection Templates remain fully fillable with zero network calls required to complete and locally save a Finding.
112	- A device with no connectivity for 5 full days shows no data loss or forced-login interruption blocking continued inspection work.
113	
114	#### FR-2: Per-field provenance
115	Every field value on every record carries the identity of the user and device that last wrote it, and the timestamp of that write, retained as history rather than overwritten.
116	**Consequences (testable):**
117	- Any field's current value can be traced to a specific (user, device, timestamp) triple via the audit view (FR-23).
118	- Overwriting a field's value does not delete the prior (user, device, timestamp, value) entry — it is retained as history.
119	
120	#### FR-3: Deterministic conflict resolution
121	At Sync Cycle time, the system compares each field's BASE (last commonly-synced value), YOURS (local edit), and THEIRS (current server value); fields changed on only one side merge automatically, and only fields changed on both sides since BASE are flagged as a Conflict for manual resolution.
122	**Consequences (testable):**
123	- Two offline edits to different fields of the same record both survive a sync with no manual intervention.
124	- Two offline edits to the *same* field of the same record by different users produce exactly one Conflict entry, never a silent overwrite of either value.
125	- Fields marked as derived/calculated in a template are excluded from field-level auto-merge and always route to manual review if touched on both sides. `[ASSUMPTION: no derived/calculated fields are defined in the four v1 templates, so this exclusion has no immediate effect but is specified to avoid silent corruption if templates gain calculated fields later.]`
126	
127	#### FR-4: Sync performance
128	A full day's queued data for one device — up to 200 Findings with attached photos — completes syncing within 90 seconds against the reference weak-LTE profile defined in §6 Cross-Cutting NFRs.
129	**Consequences (testable):**
130	- Photos are compressed on-device (FR-14) and queued before sync begins, not compressed during sync.
131	- Sync transmits only changed fields/attachments per record (delta sync), not a full-record re-upload, to meet the 90-second target. `[ASSUMPTION: delta/field-level sync is necessary to hit this target per offline-sync research; full-record sync was found in comparable products to be the usual bottleneck.]`
132	
133	#### FR-5: Sync status visibility
134	Field and supervisor UIs display per-record sync state (queued, syncing, synced, conflict) at all times.
135	**Consequences (testable):**
136	- An inspector can distinguish a locally-saved-but-unsynced Finding from a confirmed-synced one without leaving the Finding list view.
137	- A Finding in "conflict" state is visually distinguishable from "queued" and cannot be mistaken for successfully submitted.
138	
139	### 4.2 Asset Identification & Lookup
140	
141	**Description:** Inspectors must be able to identify the correct Asset without typing anything from memory, under three different field conditions: a readable tag, no tag but a map, or neither. Realizes UJ-1.
142	
143	**Functional Requirements:**
144	
145	#### FR-6: Scan-based lookup
146	An inspector can identify an Asset by scanning its QR code or NFC tag, resolving to the cached Asset record even with no connectivity.
147	**Consequences (testable):**
148	- Scanning a tag for an Asset pre-synced to the device resolves to the correct Asset record in under 2 seconds with no network call.
149	- Scanning an unrecognized or damaged tag surfaces a clear fallback prompt to map-based or nearest-N lookup rather than a dead end.
150	
151	#### FR-7: Map-based lookup (offline-capable)
152	An inspector can locate and select an Asset from a map view showing cached Asset positions and basemap tiles, without connectivity. `[ASSUMPTION: offline *viewing* of pre-synced maps/asset layers is in scope for v1 — only offline map *authoring* was named out of scope by the user; basemap tiles and Asset layers for an inspector's assigned Routes/District are pre-synced whenever the device has connectivity.]`
153	**Consequences (testable):**
154	- With no connectivity, an inspector can open the map view and see Asset pins for every Asset on their currently assigned Route.
155	- Selecting a pin opens the same Asset record FR-6 would have resolved to.
156	
157	#### FR-8: Nearest-N lookup
158	An inspector can request the N nearest Assets (N configurable per deployment) to their current GPS position when scan and map identification aren't viable (e.g., missing/damaged tag, position not on today's Route).
159	**Consequences (testable):**
160	- The nearest-N list returns Assets sorted by distance from current position, resolvable even with degraded GPS accuracy (using best-available fix).
161	- Selecting an Asset from the list opens the same Asset record as FR-6/FR-7.
162	
163	#### FR-9: GPS capture with accuracy radius
164	Every location-bearing record captures GPS coordinates and the device-reported accuracy radius at time of capture.
165	**Consequences (testable):**
166	- Every Finding stores a coordinate pair and a numeric accuracy-radius value, both visible in the audit view.
167	- GPS is captured on-demand at the moment of Asset identification/Finding creation, not via continuous background tracking. `[ASSUMPTION: fix-on-capture rather than continuous tracking, to meet the <15%/8hr battery NFR per research — continuous high-accuracy GPS was flagged as a major, avoidable drain.]`
168	
169	#### FR-10: Snap-to-asset correction
170	When captured GPS falls within a configured tolerance of a known Asset's registered location, the system offers a one-tap correction anchoring the Finding to that Asset's registered coordinates instead of the raw GPS fix.
171	**Consequences (testable):**
172	- Within tolerance, "snap to asset" is offered as a single tap and, once accepted, the Finding's recorded location is the Asset's registered coordinate, with the raw GPS fix and accuracy radius retained alongside it for audit purposes (not discarded).
173	- No free-text manual coordinate entry is offered as an alternative path, in either in- or out-of-tolerance cases. `[ASSUMPTION: removing manual coordinate typing entirely, rather than offering it as a fallback, best serves the stated goal of eliminating "typed from memory" GPS errors — out-of-tolerance cases fall back to the raw captured fix, not manual entry.]`
174	
175	### 4.3 Inspection Templates & Evidence Capture
176	
177	**Description:** The actual inspection workflows inspectors run, and the evidence discipline that makes a Finding defensible later. Realizes UJ-1.
178	
179	**Functional Requirements:**
180	
181	#### FR-11: Configurable inspection templates
182	An administrator can configure an Inspection Template's fields, required evidence, and pass/fail tolerances without code changes. V1 ships four built-in templates: Hydrant Flow Test, Valve Exercise, Main-Break Triage, Backflow-Preventer Test.
183	**Consequences (testable):**
184	- All four v1 templates are usable out of the box with no configuration required before first use.
185	- An administrator can add, remove, or re-tolerance a field on an existing template through the web app without a code deployment.
186	
187	#### FR-12: Valve exercise fields
188	The Valve Exercise template captures Turn Count and Torque readings and evaluates them against Asset-specific expected ranges.
189	**Consequences (testable):**
190	- Submitting a Torque reading outside the configured tolerance for that Asset marks the Finding an Exception (FR-20) before submission completes.
191	- Turn Count and Torque are both individually retained with Provenance (FR-2), not collapsed into a single pass/fail flag.
192	
193	#### FR-13: Required photo evidence
194	A template can mark photo capture as required; submission is blocked until the required photo(s) are attached.
195	**Consequences (testable):**
196	- Attempting to submit a Finding missing a template-required photo is blocked with a clear in-app message identifying what's missing.
197	- Once attached, the required photo cannot be submitted without its embedded EXIF metadata intact (FR-14).
198	
199	#### FR-14: On-device photo compression
200	Captured photos (up to 12MP source resolution) are compressed on-device before being queued for sync, while preserving embedded EXIF (GPS, timestamp, device) for chain-of-custody.
201	**Consequences (testable):**
202	- A 12MP source photo is reduced to a long-edge resolution and JPEG quality that preserves visual evidentiary quality while materially reducing sync payload size. `[ASSUMPTION: target ~2000-3000px long edge at ~70-85% JPEG quality, per industry-convergent practice found in research — no utility-specific evidentiary standard was identified, so this is a starting point subject to pilot validation.]`
203	- Compression happens exactly once, at capture time; a photo is never recompressed on subsequent sync retries or handling, consistent with chain-of-custody practice.
204	
205	#### FR-15: Signature capture
206	A template can require an on-screen signature (inspector, and optionally a witness or property owner) attached to the Finding.
207	**Consequences (testable):**
208	- A template configured to require a signature blocks submission until it's captured, the same way FR-13 blocks on a missing required photo.
209	- The captured signature is stored as part of the immutable Finding record with the same Provenance treatment as any other field.
210	
211	#### FR-16: Accessibility of field capture
212	The field UI supports large touch targets and a high-contrast display mode suitable for gloved hands and direct sunlight.
213	**Consequences (testable):**
214	- All primary actions (template field entry, photo capture, signature, submit) meet a minimum touch-target size usable reliably with work gloves.
215	- High-contrast mode is toggleable and meets a contrast ratio usable in direct outdoor sunlight on the target rugged-device displays.
216	
217	### 4.4 Route Planning & Dispatch
218	
219	**Description:** How dispatchers turn a list of due/overdue Assets into assignable work for specific crews. Realizes UJ-2.
220	
221	**Functional Requirements:**
222	
223	#### FR-17: Batch route planning
224	A dispatcher/supervisor can generate a Route that batches nearby due/overdue Assets for a given Crew and date.
225	**Consequences (testable):**
226	- Generating a Route for a Crew/date returns a set of geographically clustered due/overdue Assets rather than an unordered list.
227	- A generated Route is editable before being published to the Crew's devices.
228	
229	#### FR-18: Crew/equipment matching
230	The route planner excludes Assets a Crew isn't certified for or a Crew's truck isn't equipped to inspect (e.g., a Backflow-Preventer Test isn't assigned to a Crew without a certified tester and the right equipment).
231	**Consequences (testable):**
232	- A Crew lacking a configured certification never receives an Asset requiring that certification in a generated Route.
233	- Overriding this exclusion requires an explicit manual reassignment (FR-19), not a silent planner bypass.
234	
235	#### FR-19: Route reassignment
236	A dispatcher can manually reassign an Asset from one Route/Crew to another before or during the day.
237	**Consequences (testable):**
238	- Reassigning an Asset removes it from the original Crew's device view and adds it to the new Crew's, reflected on next sync.
239	- A reassignment is itself an audited action (FR-23), attributable to the dispatcher who made it.
240	
241	### 4.5 Supervisor Review & Exception Triage
242	
243	**Description:** The review workflow that lets a supervisor cover far more ground than reading every Finding — only Exceptions reach them. Realizes UJ-2.
244	
245	**Functional Requirements:**
246	
247	#### FR-20: Exception-based review queue
248	The supervisor Review Queue surfaces only Findings that are out-of-tolerance per their Template's configured thresholds, or carry an unresolved Conflict — not every submitted Finding.
249	**Consequences (testable):**
250	- A Finding within tolerance and with no Conflict never appears in the Review Queue.
251	- An out-of-tolerance Finding or a Conflicted Finding always appears, with the reason it was flagged visible at a glance.
252	
253	#### FR-21: Finding disposition
254	A supervisor can approve, reject-with-reason, or escalate-to-work-order a flagged Finding.
255	**Consequences (testable):**
256	- Each disposition action is recorded against the Finding with the supervisor's identity and timestamp (feeding FR-23).
257	- "Reject" requires a reason to be entered before the action completes.
258	
259	#### FR-22: Exception notifications
260	Supervisors receive an in-app and email notification when a new Exception enters their Review Queue. `[ASSUMPTION: in-app + email covers v1; SMS/push-to-phone for time-sensitive exceptions (e.g., a failed backflow test) is deferred pending confirmation of how time-sensitive these actually need to be — see §8 Open Questions.]`
261	**Consequences (testable):**
262	- A new Exception triggers exactly one email and one in-app notification to the Finding's assigned supervisor, not a notification per minor field within it.
263	- Notification delivery failure (e.g., bad email address) is logged and surfaced to an administrator rather than silently dropped.
264	
265	### 4.6 Audit Trail & Regulatory Reporting
266	
267	**Description:** What makes a Finding usable as evidence months or years later, and how that evidence gets bundled for a regulator. Realizes UJ-3.
268	
269	**Functional Requirements:**
270	
271	#### FR-23: Immutable audit log
272	Every create/edit/approve/export action across Findings, Assets, and Work Orders is appended to an immutable, append-only audit log; corrections are recorded as new entries with reason codes, never overwriting prior values.
273	**Consequences (testable):**
274	- Editing a previously-submitted Finding's field produces a new audit-log entry with a reason code, while the prior entry remains readable, not deleted.
275	- The audit log cannot be edited or deleted through any application-level action available to any role, including administrator.
276	
277	#### FR-24: Regulatory packet export
278	An auditor can generate a Regulatory Packet (PDF narrative + CSV data) scoped to a Reporting Period and Inspection Template type.
279	**Consequences (testable):**
280	- Selecting a Reporting Period and Template type produces a PDF and a CSV covering exactly the Findings of that type completed within that period.
281	- The export completes and is downloadable without requiring any manual data assembly outside the app.
282	
283	#### FR-25: Evidence bundling in export
284	The Regulatory Packet includes, per Finding: inspector identity, timestamp, GPS-verified location, equipment used (including calibration date where applicable), raw readings and pass/fail determination, and attached photos.
285	**Consequences (testable):**
286	- Every Finding in an exported packet shows all six evidence elements with no "data not available" gaps for Findings captured through the app.
287	- Equipment calibration date is present for any Template field that designates calibrated-equipment evidence (e.g., torque wrench, flow gauge). `[ASSUMPTION: equipment/calibration metadata is entered or selected by the inspector at capture time from a utility-maintained equipment register — the mechanism for maintaining that register is not yet specified; see §8 Open Questions.]`
288	
289	#### FR-26: Audit log and record retention
290	The audit log and underlying records are retained per a utility-configurable retention policy.
291	**Consequences (testable):**
292	- A utility can configure a retention period at or above a 7-year default floor. `[ASSUMPTION: 7-year default, informed by typical multi-year audit/asset-management cycles found in research (AWWA/GASB-adjacent practice); no single confirmed statutory number applies across states — treat as a starting default pending each pilot city's actual requirement.]`
293	- No record subject to an active retention policy can be purged, by any role, before its retention period elapses.
294	
295	### 4.7 Asset Register & Work-Order Integration
296	
297	**Description:** How Tidewatch stays a field layer on top of each utility's existing systems of record rather than becoming a second, competing one. Realizes UJ-4, UJ-2.
298	
299	**Functional Requirements:**
300	
301	#### FR-27: Two-way asset register sync
302	The system synchronizes Asset records bidirectionally with the utility's GIS feature service (Esri-compatible); field-discovered corrections write back only after GIS analyst review and approval.
303	**Consequences (testable):**
304	- A field-discovered Asset-location discrepancy generates a pending write-back proposal visible to a GIS analyst, not an automatic commit to the feature service.
305	- Approving a proposal commits the change to the feature service and records the approver via Provenance; rejecting it discards the proposed change without touching the register.
306	- `[ASSUMPTION: approval-gated write-back, rather than auto-commit, given the Asset Register is explicitly the utility's system of record and research found existing GIS-native tools treat it the same way (versioned-geodatabase reconcile workflows).]`
307	
308	#### FR-28: Work-order creation
309	An escalated Finding (FR-21) can generate a Work Order via a generic REST adapter to the utility's work-order system, or via CSV export/import when no API integration exists.
310	**Consequences (testable):**
311	- Escalating a Finding with an active REST integration configured creates a corresponding Work Order in the external system within the integration's normal latency, without manual re-entry.
312	- With no REST integration configured, the same escalation produces a CSV row in a scheduled/on-demand export containing the same Finding data.
313	
314	#### FR-29: Integration failure handling
315	If an Asset-register or work-order integration endpoint is unreachable, pending sync operations queue and retry, surfaced via a status view rather than silently dropping.
316	**Consequences (testable):**
317	- A failed write-back or work-order creation attempt is retried automatically and shows as "pending/retrying" in a status view visible to a GIS analyst or administrator.
318	- No pending integration operation is ever silently discarded; every failure path ends in either success or a visible, actionable "failed" state.
319	
320	### 4.8 Identity, Access & Contractor Management
321	
322	**Description:** Who gets into the system, what they can do once they're in, and how access ends cleanly when it should. Realizes UJ-5.
323	
324	**Functional Requirements:**
325	
326	#### FR-30: SSO authentication
327	Users authenticate via the utility's identity provider using a standard SSO protocol. `[ASSUMPTION: standards-based SAML/OIDC support is sufficient for v1 rather than bespoke per-IdP integrations — specific pilot-city IdPs (Azure AD, Okta, ADFS, etc.) are unconfirmed; see §8 Open Questions.]`
328	**Consequences (testable):**
329	- A user provisioned in the utility's IdP can authenticate into Tidewatch without a separate Tidewatch-managed password.
330	- Deactivating a user in the utility's IdP revokes their Tidewatch access on next token refresh at the latest.
331	
332	#### FR-31: Role-based access control
333	The system enforces role-scoped permissions for Field Inspector, Supervisor/Dispatcher, Auditor, GIS Analyst, and Contractor roles, each restricted to the actions/data their role requires.
334	**Consequences (testable):**
335	- A Field Inspector cannot access the Review Queue, Regulatory Packet export, or Asset Register write-back approval screens.
336	- A Contractor account (FR-33) cannot access roles' screens/data outside its configured District and Template scope, even with a valid session.
337	
338	#### FR-32: Device-bound tokens & remote wipe
339	Authentication tokens are bound to the registered device; an administrator can remotely revoke a device's access and wipe its locally cached data.
340	**Consequences (testable):**
341	- A token issued to one device cannot be used to authenticate from a different, unregistered device.
342	- Triggering remote wipe on a device clears its locally cached Findings, Asset data, and credentials on next connectivity, and the device can no longer sync until re-registered.
343	
344	#### FR-33: Contractor time-boxed accounts
345	An administrator can provision a Contractor account scoped to specific Assets/Districts and Templates, with an expiration date/time after which access is automatically revoked.
346	**Consequences (testable):**
347	- A Contractor account's access ends automatically at its configured expiration, with no administrator action required at expiry time.
348	- A Contractor account can only see/act on the Districts and Templates explicitly configured for it. `[ASSUMPTION: default maximum expiration of 90 days, administrator-configurable shorter or longer per engagement, pending confirmation of typical contractor engagement length.]`
349	
350	### 4.9 Cadence Compliance Analytics
351	
352	**Description:** The view that answers "are we actually keeping up with the valve-exercise program," which today nobody can answer without manually counting paper. Realizes the business goal in §1 Vision directly, rather than a specific UJ.
353	
354	**Functional Requirements:**
355	
356	#### FR-34: Cadence compliance dashboard
357	Supervisors/managers can view the percentage of Assets of a given type (starting with valves) exercised/tested on schedule, broken out by District.
358	**Consequences (testable):**
359	- The dashboard shows, per District, the percentage of due Assets that were inspected within their required cadence window as of the current date.
360	- Filtering by Asset type (valve, hydrant, backflow-preventer) changes the computed percentage accordingly.
361	
362	#### FR-35: Trend view
363	The dashboard shows cadence-compliance trend over a selectable Reporting Period window (e.g., trailing 12 months).
364	**Consequences (testable):**
365	- Selecting a trailing window (e.g., 12 months) renders a trend of the cadence-compliance percentage over that window, not just a current-day snapshot.
366	- The trend view's underlying data matches what a Regulatory Packet (FR-24) would report for the same period, so the two never visibly disagree.
367	
368	## 5. Non-Goals (Explicit)
369	
370	- Tidewatch is not a hydraulic modeling tool — no network simulation, pressure modeling, or capacity planning.
371	- Tidewatch is not a meter-reading/AMI system — no meter data collection or billing-adjacent functionality.
372	- Tidewatch does not cover sewer or stormwater assets in v1 — water mains only.
373	- Tidewatch is not a customer-facing product — no outage notifications or any resident-visible surface.
374	- Tidewatch does not replace the utility's GIS asset register or work-order system — it is a field layer that writes into them under review, not a competing system of record (see FR-27).
375	- Tidewatch does not support offline map *authoring* (editing basemap tiles or Asset layers from the field) — only offline *viewing* of pre-synced data (FR-7).
376	- Tidewatch does not support voice control in v1.
377	- Tidewatch does not ingest drone or robotic-crawler data in v1 — explicitly parked by the product owner as a future consideration, not a rejected one.
378	
379	## 6. Cross-Cutting NFRs
380	
381	- **Offline duration:** Full field-app functionality (FR-1) sustained for at least 5 consecutive days with zero connectivity.
382	- **Sync performance:** A 200-record day syncs within 90 seconds against a reference weak-LTE profile. `[ASSUMPTION: reference profile of ~1 Mbps downlink / 512 kbps uplink, ~150ms latency, ~1% packet loss — no utility-specific network baseline was provided; this should be validated against real pilot-site cellular conditions before launch.]`
383	- **Battery impact:** Field-app battery consumption stays under 15% of an 8-hour shift's battery budget under typical daily use (fix-on-capture GPS per FR-9, batched rather than continuous sync). `[ASSUMPTION: this target is only achievable with duty-cycled GPS and batched sync as specified — continuous background GPS tracking or continuous sync would likely exceed it, per research into comparable field apps.]`
384	- **Device support:** Rugged Android tablets (`[ASSUMPTION: Android 11+]`) and iPhones (`[ASSUMPTION: iOS 16+]`) for the field app; modern evergreen browsers for the supervisor/auditor/GIS-analyst web app.
385	- **Photo handling:** 12MP source photos compressed on-device per FR-14, EXIF-preserving.
386	- **Accessibility:** Supervisor/auditor/GIS-analyst web app meets WCAG 2.2 AA. Field app meets equivalent large-touch-target and high-contrast guidance for gloved/high-glare use (FR-16), though WCAG itself targets web content and doesn't directly certify a native field app.
387	- **Data residency:** All production data resides in-region per the deploying utility's jurisdiction. `[ASSUMPTION: "in-region" means the utility's own state/country, deployment-configurable per pilot city rather than a single fixed region — multi-city, potentially multi-region hosting is implied by selling to utilities in different jurisdictions.]`
388	- **Security:** Encryption at rest and in transit; device-bound tokens and remote wipe (FR-32); SSO via the utility's identity provider (FR-30).
389	- **Observability:** Sync failures, integration failures (FR-29), and Review Queue backlog growth are logged and alertable to operations staff.
390	- **Availability:** Supervisor/auditor/GIS-analyst web app and sync backend target `[ASSUMPTION: 99.5% uptime, excluding scheduled maintenance]` — field inspection work itself is unaffected by backend downtime since it continues fully offline (FR-1).
391	
392	## 7. Constraints and Guardrails
393	
394	**Privacy:** Tidewatch collects minimal PII — field-staff identity (tied to employment, not customer data) and occasionally property-adjacent photography incidental to an Asset's location. No customer account, billing, or usage data is collected (consistent with meter-reading/AMI being out of scope).
395	
396	**Safety:** Tidewatch is a data-capture and reporting system; it does not actuate valves, pumps, or any physical control system, so no functional-safety (e.g., IEC 61508-class) requirements apply. `[ASSUMPTION: confirm this framing holds if a future version considers any closed-loop control integration — out of scope for v1 as specified.]`
397	
398	**Cost:** No cost ceiling or pricing model was specified by the product owner; flagged as an Open Question (§8) rather than assumed, since it affects packaging decisions this PRD doesn't own.
399	
400	## 8. Stakeholders and Approvals
401	
402	Given 12-18 month municipal procurement cycles, each pilot city will likely route sign-off through several distinct stakeholders rather than a single buyer:
403	
404	- **Utility IT/Security** — SSO integration (FR-30), device management policy, data residency (§6).
405	- **GIS/Asset Management lead** — Asset Register data-model mapping and write-back approval workflow (FR-27).
406	- **Compliance/Regulatory affairs** — Regulatory Packet content (FR-24/25) sign-off against that state's actual requirements.
407	- **Field Operations director** — the likely procurement sponsor; rollout and training plan (§9) sign-off.
408	- **Union/labor representative**, where field staff are organized — device policy and any location-tracking disclosure requirements. `[ASSUMPTION: this stakeholder is relevant for at least some pilot cities given public-sector field workforces are frequently organized; confirm per city.]`
409	
410	## 9. Rollout and Change Management
411	
412	- Phased pilot in 2 cities rather than a simultaneous broad rollout.
413	- A parallel-run period (paper checklists continue alongside the app) before each city formally retires paper for valve exercising — directly de-risks the primary success metric (SM-1) by not forcing a hard cutover before trust is established.
414	- Train-the-trainer model: a small group of lead inspectors per city trained first, then extending to the full field staff.
415	- Pilot feedback loop feeds back into Inspection Template configuration (FR-11) before any wider rollout beyond the 2 pilot cities.
416	
417	## 10. Data Governance
418	
419	- **Residency:** In-region per §6.
420	- **Retention:** Per utility-configurable policy, 7-year default floor (FR-26).
421	- **Classification:** Operational/Asset data is non-PII by default; field-staff identity is the primary PII category, handled as employment-related data rather than customer data (§7 Privacy).
422	
423	## 11. Compliance and Regulatory
424	
425	This section documents the regulatory/standards context Tidewatch's audit and reporting features (§4.6) are built to satisfy — grounded in research rather than assumption, since getting this wrong undermines the product's core value proposition:
426	
427	- **Valve exercising:** No federal mandate; AWWA Manual M44 and ANSI/AWWA G200 are the industry-standard guidance utilities are generally expected to follow or exceed (typically full-system exercise within 5 years, annual for critical large-diameter valves). Individual states/utilities may set stricter cadences in their own O&M manuals.
428	- **Hydrant flow testing:** AWWA M17 and NFPA 291 govern test methodology; ISO's Public Protection Classification program is the practical commercial driver, requiring flow data no older than 5-10 years for full insurance credit.
429	- **Backflow-preventer testing:** The one area with direct state regulatory teeth — most states require annual testing by a certified tester under Safe Drinking Water Act primacy delegation, with recordkeeping requirements that vary by state. Local cross-connection-control ordinances often layer on additional device-registration and reporting obligations.
430	- **Asset-management reporting:** GASB 34's "modified approach" lets utilities skip infrastructure depreciation in financial statements if they maintain a current asset inventory, documented condition assessments via a reproducible method, evidence of a maintained condition level, and estimated annual maintenance cost — all of which §4.6's audit trail and §4.9's cadence dashboard directly support. AWWA G200/G400 series provide the underlying voluntary standards of practice for documentation and record retention.
431	- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA for the supervisor/auditor/GIS-analyst web app (§6).
432	
433	`[NOTE FOR PM: none of the above are federal mandates for valve/hydrant programs — they're industry-standard practice plus state-specific rules that vary per pilot city. Confirm each pilot city's actual state-level requirements (especially backflow testing specifics) before finalizing Regulatory Packet content with Compliance.]`
434	
435	## 12. Risk and Mitigations
436	
437	- **R1 — GPS inaccuracy underground undermines Snap-to-Asset.** Mitigated by always displaying accuracy radius (FR-9) and falling back to scan/map/nearest-N identification (§4.2) rather than forcing a low-confidence snap.
438	- **R2 — 12-18 month procurement cycles delay pilot start.** Mitigated by engaging IT/Security and Compliance stakeholders (§8) early, in parallel with commercial negotiation rather than sequentially after it.
439	- **R3 — Conflict-resolution edge cases around derived/calculated fields silently corrupt data.** Mitigated by excluding such fields from field-level auto-merge by design (FR-3), even though no v1 template currently defines one.
440	- **R4 — Crew resistance to replacing a familiar paper workflow.** Mitigated by the parallel-run rollout approach (§9) rather than a forced cutover.
441	- **R5 — GIS/work-order system variability across utilities** (Cityworks vs. Lucity vs. none, different Esri configurations). Mitigated by keeping both integrations (FR-27, FR-28) config-driven and generic rather than hard-coded to one vendor, with CSV fallback for utilities with no API-integrated work-order system.
442	- **R6 — State-specific regulatory variance** (especially backflow-testing cadence/recordkeeping). Mitigated by configurable Templates (FR-11) and retention policy (FR-26) rather than one hard-coded ruleset; see §11 note.
443	- **R7 — Battery and sync-performance NFR targets prove infeasible under real field conditions.** Mitigated by validating fix-on-capture GPS and batched/delta sync (§6) against real pilot-site network and device conditions early in the pilot, before wider rollout.
444	- **R8 — Exception-based review queue (FR-20) either misses real problems (tolerances too loose) or buries supervisors (tolerances too tight).** Mitigated by making tolerances configurable per Template (FR-11) and tracked directly via the SM-C2 counter-metric (§13).
445	
446	## 13. MVP Scope
447	
448	### 13.1 In Scope
449	
450	- Offline-first field app (Android + iOS) covering all four v1 Inspection Templates with photo/signature evidence capture, GPS/Snap-to-Asset, and scan/map/nearest-N Asset lookup.
451	- Deterministic, field-level conflict resolution and per-field provenance across all synced data.
452	- Route planning with crew/equipment matching, and a supervisor exception-based review queue with in-app/email notifications.
453	- Immutable audit log and Regulatory Packet (PDF + CSV) export.
454	- Two-way Asset Register sync (Esri-compatible, analyst-approval-gated) and Work Order creation (REST adapter + CSV fallback).
455	- SSO, RBAC across five roles, device-bound tokens with remote wipe, and time-boxed Contractor accounts.
456	- Cadence-compliance dashboard with district breakdown and trend view.
457	- Pilot rollout in 2 cities with a parallel-run period before paper retirement.
458	
459	### 13.2 Out of Scope for MVP
460	
461	- Customer-facing outage notifications — no customer-facing surface planned at all for this product line currently.
462	- Hydraulic modeling — different product category entirely.
463	- Meter reading/AMI — different asset class and workflow.
464	- Sewer and stormwater assets — deferred to a possible v2; water mains only for v1.
465	- Voice control.
466	- Offline map authoring (editing basemap/Asset layers from the field) — offline *viewing* is in scope (FR-7).
467	- Drone/robotic-crawler input sources. `[NOTE FOR PM: explicitly parked, not rejected — the product owner wants this revisited once core v1 is proven; worth a deliberate v2 scoping conversation rather than letting it default away.]`
468	- SMS notifications for exceptions — deferred pending confirmation of how time-sensitive exceptions really need to be (§8 Open Questions).
469	- Pricing/packaging model — a go-to-market concern this PRD doesn't own.
470	
471	## 14. Success Metrics
472	
473	**Primary**
474	- **SM-1:** Finding-to-work-order latency — median elapsed time from Finding submission (FR-13/FR-15 complete) to Work Order creation (FR-28), target under 4 hours in pilot cities, against a stated paper-process baseline of ~4 days. Validates FR-20, FR-21, FR-22, FR-28.
475	- **SM-2:** Paper checklist retirement — percentage of valve-exercise inspections conducted through Tidewatch rather than paper in each pilot city, target 100% by end of the parallel-run period (§9). Validates FR-11, FR-12.
476	
477	**Secondary**
478	- **SM-3:** Cadence compliance — percentage of valves (and other cadence-governed Assets) exercised/tested on schedule, by District, trending upward over the pilot. Validates FR-34, FR-35.
479	- **SM-4:** Sync reliability — percentage of field sync attempts completing within the 90-second target (§6), and overall sync success rate. Validates FR-4, FR-5.
480	- **SM-5:** Evidence completeness — percentage of Findings with all template-required evidence (photo, signature, GPS) captured, directly addressing the "photos get lost" and "GPS typed from memory" problems named in §1. Validates FR-9, FR-10, FR-13, FR-14, FR-15.
481	
482	**Counter-metrics (do not optimize)**
483	- **SM-C1:** Per-inspection time — median time from Asset identification to Finding submission must not increase versus the pre-Tidewatch paper-and-camera baseline. Counterbalances SM-1 and SM-2: a faster-to-work-order, more-complete record that takes inspectors meaningfully longer per stop isn't the win it looks like on paper.
484	- **SM-C2:** Review Queue volume per Crew-day — Exception count should not grow simply because Template tolerances (FR-11) are configured too tightly; a ballooning queue indicates false-positive triage burden on supervisors (R8), not genuine problem detection. Counterbalances SM-1 (escalation speed) and SM-3 (cadence pressure shouldn't push tolerances loose or tight for the wrong reasons).
485	
486	## 15. Open Questions
487	
488	1. Which specific GIS/work-order systems do the two actual pilot cities run (Cityworks, Lucity, ArcGIS Enterprise/Online, Maximo, something else, or nothing at all)? FR-27/FR-28 are specified generically; real integration scoping needs this confirmed per city.
489	2. What is each pilot city's actual regulatory retention requirement for backflow-testing and valve-exercise records? FR-26 defaults to 7 years pending this.
490	3. Does the field app need languages beyond English (Spanish is a common need for US utility field crews)? Assumed English + Spanish for v1 field app; confirm against actual pilot-crew demographics.
491	4. How time-sensitive do exception notifications (FR-22) really need to be? If a failed backflow test implies an active cross-connection risk, email/in-app may not be fast enough and SMS/push-to-phone should move into v1 scope.
492	5. What's the typical/maximum contractor engagement length at these utilities? FR-33 defaults to a 90-day cap pending this.
493	6. Is there a target pilot launch date or milestone, or does the timeline stay fully dependent on each city's procurement cycle (§8)?
494	7. What's the intended pricing/packaging model (per-seat, per-asset, flat enterprise license)? Not addressed in this PRD; needed before go-to-market planning.
495	8. Which identity providers do pilot cities actually run (Azure AD, Okta, ADFS, other)? FR-30 assumes standard SAML/OIDC support is sufficient.
496	9. What's the source and licensing model for offline basemap tiles (FR-7), since the utility's own GIS may or may not already provide a cacheable basemap layer?
497	10. How is the equipment/calibration register referenced in FR-25 (torque wrench, flow gauge calibration dates) maintained — inside Tidewatch, or imported from an existing calibration-tracking system?
498	11. Should drone/robotic-crawler input sources (explicitly parked, not rejected) be scoped for a defined v2, or left fully open?
499	
500	## 16. Assumptions Index
501	
502	- §4.1 FR-3 — No v1 template defines a derived/calculated field; the exclusion-from-auto-merge rule is specified defensively for future templates.
503	- §4.1 FR-4 — Delta/field-level sync (not full-record re-upload) is necessary to meet the 90-second/200-record target.
504	- §4.2 FR-7 — Offline map *viewing* (not authoring) is in scope for v1; basemap/Asset layers pre-sync whenever connectivity is available.
505	- §4.2 FR-9 — GPS is captured fix-on-demand at point of use, not via continuous background tracking, to meet the battery NFR.
506	- §4.2 FR-10 — No manual free-text coordinate entry is offered as a fallback to Snap-to-Asset; out-of-tolerance cases keep the raw captured fix.
507	- §4.3 FR-14 — Target photo compression of ~2000-3000px long edge at ~70-85% JPEG quality.
508	- §4.6 FR-25 — Equipment/calibration metadata is entered or selected by the inspector from a utility-maintained equipment register; the register's own maintenance mechanism is unspecified (see Open Question 10).
509	- §4.6 FR-26 — 7-year default retention floor, utility-configurable.
510	- §4.7 FR-27 — Asset-register write-back is analyst-approval-gated, not auto-committed.
511	- §4.8 FR-30 — Standards-based SAML/OIDC SSO is sufficient for v1; no bespoke per-IdP integration assumed.
512	- §4.8 FR-33 — 90-day default maximum Contractor-account expiration, administrator-configurable.
513	- §4.5 FR-22 — In-app + email notification channels for v1; SMS deferred.
514	- §6 — Reference weak-LTE profile (~1 Mbps down / 512 kbps up, ~150ms latency, ~1% packet loss) for the 90-second sync NFR.
515	- §6 — Battery NFR achievable only with duty-cycled GPS and batched sync, not continuous operation.
516	- §6 — Device OS floors: Android 11+, iOS 16+.
517	- §6 — Data residency means the deploying utility's own state/country, configurable per pilot city.
518	- §6 — 99.5% uptime target for the web app/sync backend, excluding scheduled maintenance.
519	- §7 — Tidewatch is framed as having no functional-safety requirements since it performs no physical control actuation.
520	- §8 — A union/labor stakeholder is relevant for at least some pilot cities with organized field workforces.
521

You are an adversarial technical reviewer examining a PRD's non-functional requirements and technical feasibility claims for internal consistency and realism.

Read the PRD at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sherifmatta-Learnings-bmad-harness/1c9f5c21-36bb-427d-a54b-af04146a506b/scratchpad/subject-sonfast/_bmad/planning-artifacts/prds/prd-tidewatch-2026-10-01/prd.md

Context: "Tidewatch" is an offline-first field inspection app for municipal water inspectors on rugged Android tablets and iPhones. Key hard constraints/NFRs: 5+ days fully offline, 12MP on-device photo compression, <15% battery per 8hr shift, 200-record day sync in <90 seconds on weak LTE, deterministic field-level conflict resolution with per-field provenance (BASE/YOURS/THEIRS 3-way comparison), two-way Esri-compatible GIS feature-service sync with analyst-approval gating, generic REST work-order adapter + CSV fallback, SSO via customer IdP with device-bound tokens and remote wipe, offline map viewing (not authoring). See §4.1, §4.2, §4.6/4.7, and §6 Cross-Cutting NFRs, §12 Risks, and §16 Assumptions Index specifically.

Adversarially probe for: (1) NFRs that are internally inconsistent or contradict each other (e.g., does "fully offline 5 days" conflict with anything about the review queue, notifications, or route planning that implicitly needs connectivity?); (2) functional requirements whose "testable consequences" aren't actually testable/verifiable as written, or that quietly assume infrastructure the PRD never specifies; (3) feasibility gaps the PRD hand-waves — e.g., is per-field conflict resolution across photo/signature *binary* attachments (not just scalar fields) actually well-specified, or does the BASE/YOURS/THEIRS model implicitly only work for scalar fields while photos/signatures are glossed over?; (4) whether the "analyst-approval-gated" GIS write-back (FR-27) and "queue and retry" integration failure handling (FR-29) could interact badly (e.g., unbounded retry queue growth, approval queue backlog never surfaced as a risk); (5) anything in §6 NFRs presented as a firm target that the PRD's own assumptions index elsewhere undermines (e.g., is a 99.5% uptime target meaningful/consistent given the offline-first architecture, or is it copied-boilerplate NFR theater?).

Be genuinely adversarial — you're looking for real holes, not confirming everything is fine. But don't flag something as a finding merely because it's tagged `[ASSUMPTION]` and deferred to an Open Question — that's working as intended in this PRD's process; flag it only if the assumption itself is internally inconsistent, infeasible, or silently missing despite being load-bearing.

Report back in under 400 words: your findings, each with a one-line failure scenario (concrete inputs/state that would break), ranked most-severe first. If something checks out fine, don't pad the report saying so — just report what you found.

Key hard constraints/NFRs: 5+ days fully offline, 12MP on-device photo compression, <15% battery per 8hr shift, 200-record day sync in <90 seconds on weak LTE, deterministic field-level conflict resolution with per-field provenance (BASE/YOURS/THEIRS 3-way comparison), two-way Esri-compatible GIS feature-service sync with analyst-approval gating, generic REST work-order adapter + CSV fallback, SSO via customer IdP with device-bound tokens and remote wipe, offline map viewing (not authoring). See §4.1, §4.2, §4.6/4.7, and §6 Cross-Cutting NFRs, §12 Risks, and §16 Assumptions Index specifically.

Adversarially probe for: (1) NFRs that are internally inconsistent or contradict each other (e.g., does "fully offline 5 days" conflict with anything about the review queue, notifications, or route planning that implicitly needs connectivity?); (2) functional requirements whose "testable consequences" aren't actually testable/verifiable as written, or that quietly assume infrastructure the PRD never specifies; (3) feasibility gaps the PRD hand-waves — e.g., is per-field conflict resolution across photo/signature *binary* attachments (not just scalar fields) actually well-specified, or does the BASE/YOURS/THEIRS model implicitly only work for scalar fields while photos/signatures are glossed over?; (4) whether the "analyst-approval-gated" GIS write-back (FR-27) and "queue and retry" integration failure handling (FR-29) could interact badly (e.g., unbounded retry queue growth, approval queue backlog never surfaced as a risk); (5) anything in §6 NFRs presented as a firm target that the PRD's own assumptions index elsewhere undermines (e.g., is a 99.5% uptime target meaningful/consistent given the offline-first architecture, or is it copied-boilerplate NFR theater?).

Be genuinely adversarial — you're looking for real holes, not confirming everything is fine. But don't flag something as a finding merely because it's tagged `[ASSUMPTION]` and deferred to an Open Question — that's working as intended in this PRD's process; flag it only if the assumption itself is internally inconsistent, infeasible, or silently missing despite being load-bearing.

Report back in under 400 words: your findings, each with a one-line failure scenario (concrete inputs/state that would break), ranked most-severe first. If something checks out fine, don't pad the report saying so — just report what you found.
